column1: Over the past century, a powerful idea has taken root in the educational landscape.
column2: 过去一个世纪里，一种颇具影响力的观念在教育领域扎下了根。
column3: Over the past century|在过去一个世纪里
column6: educational landscape|教育领域的整体面貌

column1: The concept of intelligence as something innate has been supplanted by the idea that intelligence is not fixed, and that, with the right training, we can be the authors of our own cognitive capabilities.
column2: 智力与生俱来的观念，已被另一种看法取代：智力并非固定不变，只要接受适当训练，我们就能亲自塑造自己的认知能力。

column1: Psychologist Alfred Binet, the developer of the first intelligence tests, was one of many 19th-century scientists who held that earlier view and sought to quantify cognitive ability.
column2: 心理学家阿尔弗雷德·比奈设计了最早的智力测验。在众多持第一种观点、试图量化认知能力的19世纪科学家中，他是其中之一。
column6: held that earlier view|持先前提到的观点

column1: Then, in the early 20th century, progressive thinkers revolted against the notion that inherent ability is destiny.
column2: 后来，到了20世纪初，进步思想家开始反对“天赋决定命运”这一观念。

column1: Instead, educators such as John Dewey argued that every child’s intelligence could be developed, given the right environment.
column2: 相反，约翰·杜威等教育家主张，只要环境适宜，每个孩子的智力都可以得到发展。

column1: ‘Growth mindset theory’ is a relatively new — and extremely popular — version of this idea.
column2: “成长型思维理论”是这种观念一种较新、也极受欢迎的表述。
column3: Growth mindset theory|成长型思维理论

column1: In many schools today you will see hallways covered in motivational posters and hear speeches on the mindset of great sporting heroes who simply believed their way to the top.
column2: 如今走进许多学校，你会看到走廊贴满励志海报，也会听到演讲者谈论体育明星的思维方式，称他们单凭信念就登上了顶峰。
column8: believed their way to the top|凭借信念登上顶峰

column1: A major focus of the growth mindset in schools is coaxing students away from seeing failure as an indication of their ability, and towards seeing it as a chance to improve that ability.
column2: 学校推行成长型思维的一大重点，是循循善诱，让学生不再把失败看作能力高低的标志，转而将它视为提高这种能力的机会。

column1: As educationalist Jeff Howard noted several decades ago: ‘Smart is not something that you just are, smart is something that you can get.’
column2: 正如教育学家杰夫·霍华德在几十年前所说：“聪明并不是生来如此，你也可以变得聪明。”

column1: The idea of the growth mindset is based on the work of psychologist Carol Dweck in California in the 1990s.
column2: 成长型思维这个概念源于心理学家卡罗尔·德韦克在20世纪90年代于加利福尼亚开展的研究。

column1: In one key experiment, Dweck divided a group of 10- to 12-year-olds into two groups.
column2: 在一项关键实验中，德韦克把一批10至12岁的孩子分成了两组。

column1: All were told that they had achieved a high score on a test but the first group were praised for their intelligence in achieving this, while the others were praised for their effort.
column2: 所有孩子都被告知自己在一项测验中得了高分，但第一组得到的表扬是他们聪明，所以能取得这样的成绩；另一组受表扬的则是他们付出的努力。

column1: The second group — those who had been instilled with a ‘growth mindset’ — were subsequently far more likely to put effort into future tasks.
column2: 随后，第二组，也就是被引导形成“成长型思维”的孩子，在后续任务中付出努力的可能性要大得多。
column6: far more likely|可能性大得多
column7: put effort into|把精力投入到

column1: Meanwhile, the former took on only those tasks that would not risk their sense of worth.
column2: 第一组的孩子则只肯接受那些不会危及其自我价值感的任务。

column1: This group had inferred that success or failure is due to innate ability, and this ‘fixed mindset’ had led them to fear of failure and lack of effort.
column2: 这组孩子得出结论，成败取决于天生的能力；这种“固定型思维”使他们害怕失败，也不愿付出努力。
column8: fear of failure|对失败的恐惧

column1: Praising ability actually made the students perform worse, while praising effort emphasised that change was possible.
column2: 表扬能力反而让学生表现得更差，而表扬努力则强调了人是可以改变的。

column1: One of the greatest impediments to successfully implementing a growth mindset, however, is the education system itself: in many parts of the world, the school climate is obsessed with performance in the form of constant testing, analysing and ranking of students — a key characteristic of the fixed mindset.
column2: 然而，成功推行成长型思维所面临的最大障碍之一，恰恰是教育体制本身。世界许多地方的学校过于看重表现，不停地对学生进行测验、分析和排名，而这正是固定型思维的主要特征。

column1: Nor is it unusual for schools to create a certain cognitive dissonance, when they applaud the benefits of a growth mindset but then hand out fixed target grades in lessons based on performance.
column2: 学校一面称赞成长型思维的好处，一面却又按学生的表现为其设定固定的课堂成绩目标。这种造成认知失调的做法也不罕见。
column8: fixed target grades|固定的目标成绩

column1: Aside from the implementation problem, the original growth mindset research has also received harsh criticism.
column2: 除了推行中遇到的问题，最初有关成长型思维的研究也受到了尖锐批评。

column1: The statistician Andrew Gelman claims that ‘their research designs have enough degrees of freedom that they could take their data to support just about any theory at all’.
column2: 统计学家安德鲁·格尔曼认为，“他们的研究设计留下了太多自由度，以至于他们几乎可以用自己的数据来支持任何理论”。

column1: Professor of Psychology Timothy Bates, who has been trying to replicate Dweck’s work, is finding that the results are repeatedly null.
column2: 心理学教授蒂莫西·贝茨一直试图重复德韦克的研究，但一次又一次都没有发现显著效果。
column8: null|adj. 未显示显著效果的

column1: He notes that: ‘People with a growth mindset don’t cope any better with failure ...
column2: 他指出：“有成长型思维的人并不更善于应对失败……

column1: Kids with the growth mindset aren’t getting better grades, either before or after our intervention study.’
column2: 不论在我们的干预研究之前还是之后，有成长型思维的孩子也都没有取得更好的成绩。”
column5: either before or after|无论在……之前还是之后

column1: Much of this criticism is not lost on Dweck, and she deserves great credit for responding to it and adapting her work accordingly.
column2: 德韦克清楚其中的许多批评。她作出回应，并据此调整了自己的研究，这一点很值得肯定。
column5: deserves great credit|值得充分肯定

column1: In fact, she argues that her work has been misunderstood and misapplied in a range of ways.
column2: 实际上，她认为自己的研究在许多方面被人误解、误用了。
column7: a range of ways|多种方式

column1: She has also expressed concerns that her theories are being misappropriated in schools by being conflated with the self-esteem movement: ‘For me the growth mindset is a tool for learning and improvement.
column2: 她还表示担忧：学校把她的理论与提倡自尊的运动混为一谈，从而曲解了理论的用途。她说：“对我而言，成长型思维是帮助人学习和进步的工具。

column1: It’s not just a vehicle for making children feel good.’
column2: 它绝不只是用来让孩子自我感觉良好的手段。”

column1: But there is another factor at work here.
column2: 但这里还有另一个因素在起作用。

column1: The failure to translate the growth mindset into the classroom might reflect a misunderstanding of the nature of teaching and learning itself.
column2: 成长型思维未能落实到课堂，可能反映出人们对教与学本身的性质存在误解。
column4: translate|v. 把……转化为实际做法

column1: Growth mindset supporters David Yeager and Gregory Walton claim that interventions should be delivered in a subtle way to maximise their effectiveness.
column2: 成长型思维的支持者戴维·耶格尔和格雷戈里·沃尔顿认为，干预应以不露痕迹的方式实施，以最大限度地发挥作用。
column7: in a subtle way|以不易察觉的方式

column1: They say that if adolescents perceive a teacher’s intervention as conveying that they are in need of help, this could undo its intended effects.
column2: 他们说，如果青少年觉得教师的干预是在暗示自己需要帮助，干预原本希望达到的效果就可能被抵消。

column1: A lot of what drives students is their innate beliefs and how they perceive themselves.
column2: 促使学生采取行动的因素中，有很大一部分来自他们内在的信念，以及他们对自己的看法。

column1: There is a strong correlation between self-perception and achievement, but there is evidence to suggest that the actual effect of achievement on self-perception is stronger than the other way round.
column2: 自我认知与学业成就之间有很强的相关性，但有证据表明，学业成就对自我认知的实际影响，比反方向的影响更强。

column1: To stand up in a classroom and successfully deliver a good speech is a genuine achievement, and that is likely to be more powerfully motivating than vague notions of ‘motivation’ itself.
column2: 能在课堂上站起来，成功地作一次出色的演讲，是实实在在的成就。相比关于“动力”本身的模糊概念，这样的成就可能更能激励人。
column3: deliver a good speech|作一场出色的演讲

column1: Recent evidence would suggest that growth mindset interventions are not the elixir of student learning that its proponents claim it to be.
column2: 近期证据似乎表明，成长型思维干预并不像其支持者所声称的那样，是促进学生学习的灵丹妙药。

column1: The growth mindset appears to be a viable construct in the lab, which, when administered in the classroom via targeted interventions, doesn’t seem to work.
column2: 成长型思维在实验室里似乎是个可行的理论构念；可一旦通过有针对性的干预把它引入课堂，它似乎就不起作用了。

column1: It is hard to dispute that having faith in the capacity to change is a good attribute for students.
column2: 相信自己有能力改变，这对学生而言是一种好品质，恐怕很难有人反对这一点。

column1: Paradoxically, however, that aspiration is not well served by direct interventions that try to instil it.
column2: 然而，颇为矛盾的是，试图直接灌输这种信念的干预，却不能很好地实现这一愿望。

column1: Motivational posters and talks are often a waste of time, and might well give students a deluded notion of what success actually means.
column2: 励志海报和演讲往往是白费时间，而且很可能让学生对成功究竟意味着什么产生错误认识。
column5: a waste of time|浪费时间

column1: Teaching concrete skills such as how to write an effective introduction to an essay then praising students’ effort in getting there is probably a far better way of improving confidence than telling them how unique they are, or indeed how capable they are of changing their own brains.
column2: 教学生一些具体技能，比如如何为文章写出有力的引言，然后表扬他们为学会这项技能所付出的努力，这可能比告诉他们自己多么与众不同，或多么有能力改变自己的大脑，更能增强他们的信心。

column1: Perhaps growth mindset works best as a philosophy and not an intervention.
column2: 也许把成长型思维当作一种理念，而非一项干预措施，最能发挥它的作用。
